quests.instruction: You notice the moon looks different than it did last night. How do you feel?
quests.question: Curious
quests.hint: Spotting a change in something you see every night can make you want to ask why.
quests.explanation: Spotting a change in something familiar makes you want to ask questions and find out why.
quests.funFact: The moon changes shape in the sky every night because of its journey around the Earth!

quests.instruction: You try to walk like a penguin all the way across the room. How do you feel?
quests.question: Silly
quests.hint: Waddling around on purpose to make people laugh is a very playful choice.
quests.explanation: Waddling around like a penguin on purpose is a playful, giggly way to make people smile.
quests.funFact: Real penguins waddle because their short legs are set far back on their round bodies!

quests.instruction: You pet your cat slowly while it purrs softly on your lap. How do you feel?
quests.question: Calm
quests.hint: Slow, gentle petting and a soft purring sound can help your body settle down.
quests.explanation: Slow, gentle petting and a soft purring sound can help your whole body feel settled.
quests.funFact: A cat's purr happens at a steady rhythm that many people find very soothing!

quests.instruction: Your pet has not come home yet and it is almost dark. How do you feel?
quests.question: Worried
quests.hint: Not knowing where a pet you love has gone can make your chest feel tight.
quests.explanation: Not knowing where a pet you love has wandered off to can give you an uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Calling a pet's name in a calm, happy voice often helps them find their way home.

quests.instruction: You are the only one in your family who is awake this early in the morning. How do you feel?
quests.question: Lonely
quests.hint: Being the only one awake in a quiet house can feel a little empty.
quests.explanation: Being the only one awake in a quiet house can give you a quiet, empty kind of feeling.
quests.funFact: Quiet mornings can also be a peaceful time to read or draw until everyone wakes up!

quests.instruction: The weather forecast says it might snow enough for a snow day tomorrow. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: The chance of an unexpected day of fun can make you want to check outside again and again.
quests.explanation: The chance of an unexpected snow day fills you with bouncy, hopeful energy.
quests.funFact: Many kids check the window first thing in the morning to see if snow day dreams came true!

quests.instruction: Your whole class claps for you after your presentation. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: Hearing everyone clap just for you can make your smile grow really big.
quests.explanation: Hearing your classmates clap for you after your hard work is a warm, happy moment.
quests.funFact: Clapping is a way people all over the world show they are proud of you!

quests.instruction: You watch a suspenseful part of a movie where the music suddenly gets loud. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Sudden loud music during a tense scene can make you grip your seat.
quests.explanation: Sudden loud music during a tense part of a movie can give you a quick, jumpy feeling.
quests.funFact: Movie makers use loud, sudden music on purpose to make a scene feel extra thrilling!

quests.instruction: You walk outside and see that it snowed overnight. How do you feel?
quests.question: Surprised
quests.hint: Seeing the whole world look different overnight can make your eyes go wide.
quests.explanation: Seeing the whole world look different overnight, like fresh snow, gives you a burst of surprise.
quests.funFact: Snowflakes form in the sky and each one has its own unique, tiny pattern!

quests.instruction: You help your teacher pass out papers to the whole class. How do you feel?
quests.question: Proud
quests.hint: Being trusted with a helpful job in front of the class can feel really good.
quests.explanation: Being trusted with a helpful job in front of the class gives you a warm feeling of accomplishment.
quests.funFact: Helping out in the classroom is a great way to feel like an important part of the team!

quests.instruction: You see footprints in the snow that do not look like yours. How do you feel?
quests.question: Curious
quests.hint: Spotting a mystery trail can make you want to follow it and figure out the answer.
quests.explanation: Spotting a mysterious trail makes you want to follow it and figure out where it leads.
quests.funFact: Animal tracks in snow can tell you what kind of animal passed by and which way it went!

quests.instruction: You and your friend make up your own made-up language just for fun. How do you feel?
quests.question: Silly
quests.hint: Inventing funny nonsense words together with a friend is a very giggly game.
quests.explanation: Inventing funny nonsense words with a friend is a playful, giggly kind of game.
quests.funFact: Inventing words and sounds is something even real language experts enjoy doing for fun!

quests.instruction: You breathe slowly after a short, quiet breathing exercise with your class. How do you feel?
quests.question: Calm
quests.hint: A few slow, deep breaths together can help everyone's body settle down.
quests.explanation: A few slow, deep breaths together can help your whole body feel settled and quiet.
quests.funFact: Many classrooms practice slow breathing together to help everyone feel ready to learn.

quests.instruction: You have a big spelling test tomorrow that you have not studied for yet. How do you feel?
quests.question: Worried
quests.hint: Thinking about something important coming up that you are not ready for can feel uneasy.
quests.explanation: Thinking about a big test you have not studied for yet can give you an uneasy, fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Studying for even ten minutes can help this uneasy feeling turn into confidence!

quests.instruction: You spend the whole afternoon at home with no one to talk to. How do you feel?
quests.question: Lonely
quests.hint: A long, quiet afternoon with no one around can feel a little empty.
quests.explanation: A long, quiet afternoon with no one to talk to can leave you with an empty feeling.
quests.funFact: A phone call or video chat with someone you love can help this feeling fade quickly!

quests.instruction: You hear that your cousins are coming to stay for the whole weekend. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: Thinking about a whole weekend of playing together can make you count the days.
quests.explanation: Thinking about a whole weekend of playing with cousins fills you with eager, happy energy.
quests.funFact: Planning games ahead of time can make a visit with cousins even more fun!

quests.instruction: You get to stay up a little later than usual on a special weekend night. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: A special treat like extra time before bed can make you smile.
quests.explanation: A special treat, like extra time before bed, is a simple, happy little moment.
quests.funFact: Special little treats like this can make weekends feel extra fun!

quests.instruction: You hear your name called out unexpectedly in a quiet room. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: A sudden sound breaking a long silence can make you jump a little.
quests.explanation: A sudden sound breaking a long silence can give you a quick, jumpy feeling.
quests.funFact: Our bodies are wired to notice sudden sounds quickly, even in a quiet room!

quests.instruction: Your parents tell you that you are going somewhere secret today. How do you feel?
quests.question: Surprised
quests.hint: Not knowing where you are headed can make you gasp with wonder.
quests.explanation: Not knowing where you are headed but knowing it is a secret gives you a fun jolt of surprise.
quests.funFact: Mystery trips are a fun way families create memories that feel extra exciting!

quests.instruction: You finish a long hike all the way to the top without stopping. How do you feel?
quests.question: Proud
quests.hint: Reaching the top after a long, hard climb feels like a big personal win.
quests.explanation: Reaching the top after a long, hard climb gives you a warm feeling of accomplishment.
quests.funFact: Hiking builds strong legs and a strong sense of 'I can do hard things!'

quests.instruction: You spot a rainbow and wonder how it got its colors. How do you feel?
quests.question: Curious
quests.hint: Noticing something beautiful in the sky can make you want to know the reason behind it.
quests.explanation: Noticing something beautiful and unusual makes you want to ask questions about how it happens.
quests.funFact: Rainbows appear when sunlight bends through raindrops and splits into different colors!

quests.instruction: You put googly eyes on all the fruit in the kitchen. How do you feel?
quests.question: Silly
quests.hint: Turning ordinary things into something goofy and funny brings on the giggles.
quests.explanation: Turning ordinary fruit into something goofy and funny is a playful, giggly little joke.
quests.funFact: Adding a silly twist to everyday things is a fun way to practice being creative!

quests.instruction: You lie in the grass and watch the clouds drift slowly by. How do you feel?
quests.question: Calm
quests.hint: Watching clouds move slowly across the sky can help your thoughts slow down too.
quests.explanation: Watching clouds drift slowly across the sky can help your thoughts feel settled and quiet.
quests.funFact: Clouds drift because they float along with the wind high up in the sky!

quests.instruction: You cannot find your homework right before class starts. How do you feel?
quests.question: Worried
quests.hint: Not knowing where something important is can make your tummy feel tight.
quests.explanation: Not being able to find something important right when you need it can give you a tight, uneasy feeling.
quests.funFact: Taking a slow breath and retracing your steps can help you find lost things and feel calmer.

quests.instruction: Your cousins go home after visiting and the house feels very quiet. How do you feel?
quests.question: Lonely
quests.hint: A house that was full of noise and laughter can feel extra empty once everyone leaves.
quests.explanation: A house that was full of laughter can feel quiet and a little empty once everyone leaves.
quests.funFact: Looking at photos from the visit is a nice way to remember the fun while you wait to see them again!

quests.instruction: You hear a strange new sound coming from the kitchen. How do you feel?
quests.question: Curious
quests.hint: A sound you cannot recognize yet can make you want to go investigate.
quests.explanation: Hearing a sound you cannot recognize yet makes you want to go find out what it is.
quests.funFact: Being curious about new sounds is one of the ways scientists start their best questions!

quests.instruction: You put your socks on your hands and pretend they are talking puppets. How do you feel?
quests.question: Silly
quests.hint: Turning laundry into playful little puppet characters feels like a fun, goofy game.
quests.explanation: Turning ordinary socks into playful puppet characters is a fun, giggly bit of pretend play.
quests.funFact: Sock puppets have been a favorite make-believe toy for kids for generations!

quests.instruction: You sit quietly by the window and watch the rain fall. How do you feel?
quests.question: Calm
quests.hint: Watching something gentle and steady can help your mind slow down.
quests.explanation: Watching something gentle and steady, like falling rain, helps your mind feel settled.
quests.funFact: The steady sound of rain is a favorite relaxing sound for many people!

quests.instruction: You forgot to bring your permission slip and the field trip is tomorrow. How do you feel?
quests.question: Worried
quests.hint: Forgetting something important that you need for tomorrow can give your stomach a little flutter.
quests.explanation: Forgetting something important that you need soon can give you an uneasy, fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking a teacher for help right away is a great way to fix a forgotten form quickly.

quests.instruction: Everyone in class already has a partner for the project except you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Lonely
quests.hint: Being the only one without a partner for a project can feel quiet and empty.
quests.explanation: Being the only one without a partner can leave you with a quiet, empty kind of feeling.
quests.funFact: Teachers are usually happy to help find you a group when this happens — just ask!
